{{short description|American biostatistician}}
'''Vicki Stover Hertzberg''' is an American [[biostatistics|biostatistician]], who is currently professor in the [[Nell Hodgson Woodruff School of Nursing]] of Emory University, where she founded and continues to direct its Center for Data Science. Previously she worked as a professor of biostatistics and bioinformatics in the [[Rollins School of Public Health]] of [[Emory University]] between 1994 and 2015, serving as the department chair 1994-2001. {{r|cv}}

==Education and career==
Hertzberg studied mathematics and statistics at [[Miami University]] of Ohio, graduating in 1976.{{r|cv}} She completed a PhD in biomathematics and health statistics in 1980 at the [[University of Washington]]. Her dissertation, ''Inter-Viewer Variability in Assessing Coronary Arteriography: A Statistical Model'', was supervised by Lloyd Fisher.{{r|mgp}}
Next, she joined the faculty at the [[University of Cincinnati]], where she remained until her 1995 move to Emory.{{r|cv}} At Emory, she chaired the Department of Biostatistics and Bioinformatics from 1994 to 2001.{{r|c50}}

==Awards and honors==
Hertzberg won [[American Statistical Association Founders Award]] in 1994.{{r|fa}} She has been a [[fellow of the American Statistical Association]] since 1999,{{r|fasa}}. She was one of the first American Statistical Association members to gain the P.Stat. certification designation.{{r|cv}}
